decisionBasis: 150m leaves only about 1.7m between Expo representative point and one public auxiliary route minimum, and only 1-3.2s minimum synthetic lead across noise/rate groups.
300m increases synthetic minimum lead to 7-9.2s across noise/rate groups while retaining a smaller surrounding area than 500m; 500m gives more lead but no additional accepted synthetic trials.
180 seconds is an explicit demo operating tradeoff between 60/300 seconds, not an empirically optimal cooldown. Tests independently enforce post-cooldown new measured outside exit and new approach.
64-point fresh observation window fixes adjacent-pair cadence blindness without lowering distance uncertainty thresholds. Any definite recession overrides an older net approach.
limits: POI representative point is not surveyed accuracy, entrance, road access, vehicle visibility or legal-route evidence.
The synthetic meridian crosses the point; it does not predict actual road approach times. NAVER proximity is separate auxiliary geometry evidence.
Both places accept 34/36 selected synthetic conditions. The 5m/s,30m accuracy,zero-error condition remains missed at both sample rates because 10 seconds cannot separate uncertainty.
Bounded noise is not a guarantee about statistical Android accuracy. Smaller-than-uncertainty turns cannot be instantly identified.
Lead is to the sampled closest point, not guaranteed output start or completion; story/music/interruption boundaries may legitimately discard an encounter.
UNKNOWN/ACTIVE navigation is never treated as INACTIVE. Active-route membership and actual Pleos route identity remain unimplemented.
No observed user coordinates, real driving, human speech, model call, product card creation or heard-history reset in this review.
